## INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLI INFECTION
Catheter removal is strongly recommended, especially when resistant isolates are
present. Delayed catheter removal is associated with increased mortality in
patients with drug resistant organisms. The decision about whether to remove the
catheter depends on severity of illness, presence of resistant organisms, the
need for the catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.
## Treatment if catheter is removed (preferred)
Duration of therapy
## Inpatient

Treat uncomplicated cases for 7 to 14 days. A longer duration may be required
for complicated or critically ill patients. Consult Infectious Diseases for more
information.
Treatment
Refer to specific isolate bacteremia recommendations for selection of
antimicrobial.

## Treatment if catheter removal is not possible (less desirable)
Duration of therapy
Treat uncomplicated cases with concurrent systemic and antibiotic lock therapy
for 14 days. A longer duration may be required for complicated or critically ill
patients.
## Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.
Treatment
Add antimicrobial lock therapy to systemic treatment
[<ADD> gentamicin antibiotic lock therapy](psjizid-gent-1mg-antibotic-lock-soln)
